_meta.branched_from_note: Cut once PR #5 (build/fundamentals-f1 -> master) merged, per T0's instruction -- event_fundamentals.parquet and D32 Amendment A1 are both on master as of this branch.
_meta.amendment_note: Cooper approved the plan 2026-09-13 ('approved, proceed') with two amendments made in the same exchange: T3b/T3c run undirected (not pre-registered), and no split -- including T3a -- is evaluated against a kill-condition margin ('exploratory, no kill condition'). See prompts/phase_13.md's Approval Gate section for the full account.

universe.note: Build F1's output, read directly -- not re-derived. All 9 of F1's Verification Block checks pass on this table as of the branch point.

p0_outcome.entry_reference_note: Proposed as the default (same anchor this whole programme's detection work already uses) and not challenged when posted -- adopted as written, distinct from the two items Cooper did amend.
p0_outcome.horizons_note: Matches Phase 11's named-cell horizon (hold 30 min) and Phase 9's grid -- adopted default, not separately re-confirmed.
p0_outcome.source_table_note: 45,925,350 rows, built by research/phase_6b/build_minute_bars_v2.py directly from filtered_trades/filtered_trades_dev_v4 -- same tick-derived basis as everything else this programme measures on. Checked directly 2026-09-13, not assumed.
p0_outcome.cost_unit_note: 9,017,475 rows, keyed (ticker, event_date, minute_index, segment). Round-trip cost per event = 2 x tw_spread_bp at the entry reference's minute, matching Phase 11's round-trip convention (T6/T7). Per-event, not Phase 11's 70.98bp population aggregate.
p0_outcome.reference_aggregate_note: Phase 11 T7 named cell (fixed_horizon, RTH, latency 5min, hold 30min), n=10,544, 52.86% non-positive realized capture -- population-level reference only, not the per-event denominator this phase actually uses.

arm_zero.note: Reused from F1-T6 (tick-derived detection price, D4-compliant), not rebuilt.

t3a_flg_dilution.declared_direction: events with a dilution filing before t0 show worse continuation and a faster flip than events without one
t3a_flg_dilution.direction_set_by: the architect's proposal, signed off by Cooper before the 2026-09-13 amendment -- not invented by this phase

t3b_share_turnover.construction: event volume (tick-derived) / shs_shares_outstanding, split-adjusted using spl_ history
t3b_share_turnover.note: Cooper's 2026-09-13 amendment: no pre-registered direction. Both tails reported.

kill_condition.note: Cooper's 2026-09-13 amendment: 'exploratory, no kill condition.' No split, including T3a, is evaluated against a pass/fail margin. Escalation rows 2/3 in prompts/phase_13.md hard-stop if any script or chart declares a split as having cleared, passed, or been singled out as a finding.

cross_cuts.note: Nested within year (coverage is collinear with the vendor calendar cliff, per F1-T6c) and within price decile (arm zero's control, per the design's SS5 nested-comparison instruction).

t4_tick_confirmation.triggered_by: Cooper, 2026-09-14: 'proceed with tick confg' -- confirmed via AskUserQuestion to mean T3b (share turnover), the recommended option (largest population-aggregate separation of the three splits, ~3x median MFE cost-multiple at 15min).
t4_tick_confirmation.source_table_note: Raw ticks, not event_minute_bars_v2 -- the point of T4 is to confirm the bar-derived finding holds against the tick data the bars were themselves built from, not to re-derive it from the same aggregate. build_minute_bars_v2.py applies no trade-condition/correction filter beyond filtered_trades' own contents, so this is an apples-to-apples comparison, not a stricter/looser filter.
t4_tick_confirmation.time_filter: sip_timestamp BETWEEN t0_ns AND t0_ns + horizon_minutes * 60 * 1e9, filtered on the raw BIGINT column directly (a converted-timestamp filter defeats DuckDB's row-group pruning, confirmed elsewhere in this repo)
t4_tick_confirmation.population: the 11,971 T3b-covered events (defined turnover value) -- same population t3_partitions.py's T3b split already uses, no further sampling (bulk full-table join benchmarked elsewhere in this repo at ~25 min for a heavier per-minute aggregation over 15,763 events; this single-window MAX/MIN pass is lighter).
